question: Should OpenClaw add and support `socket.drain` as a read-scoped gateway event for session-message clients, or retain the existing reconnect/reconciliation model after the linked feature request was closed as not planned?
rationale: The change introduces a new externally reachable gateway protocol event and intentionally changes teardown backpressure semantics; code review cannot determine the desired long-term delivery and recovery contract.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded event contract
options.body: Keep the feature only after defining a bounded slow-client policy, documenting client reconciliation, and proving the latest head under a saturated recipient.

options.title: Decline the new protocol event
options.body: Close the feature direction and retain existing session-change and reconnect reconciliation behavior for gateway consumers.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded event contract
recommendation.body: Keep the feature only after defining a bounded slow-client policy, documenting client reconciliation, and proving the latest head under a saturated recipient.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only human reviewer signal in the available PR discussion and are the best available candidate to route the gateway protocol decision.
